In this notebook the pure behavioural analysis is conducted.
Imports first ...

```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(readr)
library(mgcv)
library(lme4)
library(data.table)
```

Load the behavioural data from the datadir.

```{r echo=FALSE}
# Get the DATADIR environment variable and read in data
datadir <- Sys.getenv("DATADIR")
resdir <- Sys.getenv("RESDIR")
fig_path <- file.path(resdir, 'Figures', 'Main', 'behavioural_results')
behav_dir <- file.path(datadir, "derivatives", "eeg-preproc")


# subject IDs and file names
subjects <- sprintf("%03d", 13:52)
modalities <- c('elec', 'mecha')

# Pre-allocate list to store each subject's data
df_list_meta <- list()

# Load and process each subject
for (mod in modalities) {
  for (i in seq_along(subjects)) {
    
    sub_id <- subjects[i]
    write(sub_id)
    file_path_meta <- file.path(behav_dir,
      paste0("sub-", sub_id), paste0("ses-", mod),
      paste0("sub-", sub_id, "_ses-", mod, "_task-NT_allmetadata.tsv")
    )
    
    # Skip iteration if file does not exist
    if (!file.exists(file_path_meta)) {
      message(paste("No data for subject", sub_id))
      next
    }
    
    # Read large file efficiently
    df_metadata <- fread(file_path_meta, sep = "\t")
    
    # Convert intensity_level to factor and numeric
    df_metadata$intensity_level <- factor(df_metadata$intensity_level)
    df_metadata$modality <- factor(df_metadata$modality)
    df_metadata$intensity_num <- as.numeric(df_metadata$intensity_level) -1
    df_metadata$response_bin <- ifelse(df_metadata$response_decoded == "Yes", 1, ifelse(df_metadata$response_decoded == "No", 0, NaN))
    
    # exclude bad data and border intensities 
    df_metadata <- df_metadata[analysis_excluded == FALSE]

    desired_cols <- c("sub", "modality", "block", "intensity_level", "intensity_norm", "intensity_num", "response_decoded", "response_bin", "force", "force_quantile", "response_time")
  
    df_metadata <- df_metadata[, desired_cols, with = FALSE]
    df_list_meta[[length(df_list_meta) + 1]] <- df_metadata
  }
}
# Combine all into one big data.table
df_all_meta <- rbindlist(df_list_meta)
df_all_meta <- as.data.table(df_all_meta)
```

# Overview
Make some overview plots:
- How many subjects do we have per modality
```{r}
ggplot(df_all_meta[, .(num_subjects = uniqueN(sub)), by = modality], aes(x = modality, y = num_subjects)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Number of Subjects per Modality")
```
- How many trials per modality 
```{r}
ggplot(df_all_meta[, .N, by = modality], aes(x = modality, y = N)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Number of Trials per Modality")
```
- Number of trials by intensity
```{r}
ggplot(df_all_meta[, .N, by = .(intensity_level, response_decoded)], aes(x = intensity_level, y = N)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Number of Trials per Intensity")
```

- Response by force
```{r}

# Filter for modality mecha, response == "Yes", and non-missing force values
df_mecha_yes <- df_all_meta[
  modality == "Mechanical" & 
  response_decoded == "Yes" & 
  !is.na(response_decoded) & 
  !is.na(force_quantile)
]
```


# Statistical Analysis
- test if there is a statistical difference between the effect of modalities on response
- if yes, make a model separately

```{r}
# prepare data
df_all_meta <- df_all_meta[intensity_num > 1]
df_all_meta <- df_all_meta[intensity_num < 7]
sapply(df_all_meta[, .(modality, intensity_level, force)], function(x) length(levels(x)))
table(df_all_meta$modality)
table(df_all_meta$intensity_level)
table(df_all_meta$block)
df_model <- df_all_meta[!is.na(force)]

```
## Check prerequisits for using GLM analysis
Since I model binary responses, I am using the logit as a link function. 
1. Response variable is binary
2. Homogeneity of variance 
3. Independence of observations (we cannot test this here, this is an assumption we make)

```{r}
# Fit logistic regression model first
model <- glm(response_bin ~ intensity_num + modality, family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = df_all_meta)

# Create dataset with predictor and linear predictor
df_all_meta$linear_pred <- predict(model, type = "link")  # linear predictor = log-odds

# Function to plot predictor vs log-odds with smoothing curve
plot_predictor_logit <- function(df, predictor) {
  ggplot(df, aes_string(x = predictor, y = "linear_pred")) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
    labs(title = paste("Linearity check of", predictor, "vs log-odds"),
         x = predictor,
         y = "Linear predictor (log-odds)") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Plot for intensity_num
p1 <- plot_predictor_logit(df_all_meta, "intensity_num")
print(p1)

# Plot for force
p2 <- plot_predictor_logit(df_all_meta, "force")
print(p2)
```

```{r}

model2 <- glm(response_bin ~ modality * intensity_norm, family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = df_all_meta)
model3 <- glm(response_bin ~ modality * intensity_level + block, family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = df_all_meta)
```
